The strongest winds have generally been across the north west of the UK, chiefly Scotland, where gusts of over 80mph have been recorded.

There were also strong winds further south, in fact 85mph on the Isle of Wight.

Most of the rain has now cleared southern parts, but many central and western areas will see showers today, and Scotland has further showers and heavy rain to come.

Winds remain strong this morning, easing in the south this afternoon and in the north overnight.

Scottish roads closed due to fallen trees and flooding

When dangerous weather is forecast, a weather warning will be issued by the Met Office, the UK’s national weather service.

Weather warnings are given a colour – yellow, amber or red - with yellow being the lowest, and red the most serious. The colour assigned depends on a combination of two things: the impact the weather is likely to have and the likelihood of it happening.

An example of a Met Office warning matrix. Here, the position of the tick indicates that a yellow weather warning would be issued

Storm Boelo brings top wind gust of 85mph

Amber wind warnings remain in force as Storm Boelo continues to bring wet and windy weather to the UK.

The Met Office says winds peaked overnight with gusts of 60-70mph affecting some northern parts of the UK.

Gusts in some exposed coastal spots topped 80mph, with the village of Machrihanish in Argyll and Bute recording 85mph.

Four wind warnings remain in place today - two amber and two yellow - affecting most of the northern half of the UK. A yellow rain warning is still in force over parts of the Scottish Highlands.

A rain warning which stretched down to the southern part of the UK yesterday has lifted overnight.

The storm continues to disrupt transport, with Avanti West Coast advising against travelling north of Preston and LNER advising against travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen.

Cumbria Police says it received \"a number of calls overnight to localised flooding and fallen trees blocking roads\".

There are also 14 active flood warnings currently in place from the Environment Agency, affecting areas such as Cumbria, Merseyside and the prime minister's constituency of Makerfield.

We'll bring you updates throughout the day - stick with us.

Travel disruption to continue today as Storm Boelo brought gusts of 85mph overnight

The second storm in two days has brought wet and windy weather to the UK, causing travel disruption and event cancellations.

Scotland, Northern Ireland and the north of England are bracing for the worst of Storm Boelo, with gusts of up to 80mph forecast.

Three yellow weather warnings are already in place for wind and rain, impacting areas from Scotland right down to southern England.

Another three warnings will kick in this evening from 21:00, including two more serious amber warnings for wind impacting Northern Ireland, Scotland and northern England. We've got full details on those here.

Halloween events have been cancelled in Scotland and Northern Ireland, a marathon has been called off in North Wales and Knowsley Safari Park in Merseyside, north-west England, will be closed tomorrow.

National Rail has announced disruption on a number of lines, flights to and from Dublin Airport have been cancelled, and highway authorities are urging drivers to take particular care and avoid non-essential journeys.

A number of power cuts in the Glasgow and Edinburgh areas have already been reported to SP Energy Networks, while power outages continue to affect large parts of south-west England following Friday's Storm Austen.

We're pausing our live coverage now, but you can read the latest in our news story.

Second storm in two days brings travel disruption across UK

Storm Boelo follows hot on the heels of Storm Austen, but forecasts also show the potential for yet another deep area of low pressure to arrive later on Monday and into Tuesday.
